body: The implementation needs some work, but the feature itself is good IMO.

Pushed some changes from the above comments:
- refactored dialogs to reuse existing prop_selector and pick_track instead of creating new ones.
  - This change added some enum values that I put in the existing enum, not sure if that should go in a separate named enum.
- Removed redundant path_menu (right click menu), reusing the existing one.
- Added a type filter for track types that require specific node types (changing the path of an AudioPlayback track requires an AudioPlayer node, etc.)
  - Note property tracks still do not have a type filter, by design
- Fixed sub-properties getting truncated.
  - Tested with r/g/b sub properties of modulate.
- Made "Change Property" show conditionally. 
  - It will no longer appear when a track's type does not have a property. (only property, blend_shape, and bezier have a property in the path)
  - It will no longer appear if the target node path is invalid
- Added periods to sentences in comments.
- Reordered functions affected in this PR to have the same order as the header file
  - other functions in the file appear to be out of order, but it's probably unwise to move them in this PR.

Tested with Position/Rotation/Scale3D tracks (among the others), change path works and change property no longer provided as an option.
I haven't tested it with a Skeleton or bone_pose, but the tracks should be the same.
I haven't tested with a subpass, I'm not even sure what it is tbh.

> I haven't tested it with a Skeleton or bone_pose, but the tracks should be the same.

No, normal PosRotScl3D track has `./Node3D` as path, but PosRotScl3D with bone_pose uses subpaths separated by `:` like `./Skeleton3D:head`.

This is an invalid path if no bones are found in changed Skeleton3D by dialog, so validation is required.

Also, since subpaths are used not only on the Pos/Rot/Scl/Blendshape but also on the Bezier track, like `./Node2D/position:x`, it would be necessary to test on the bezier track as well.

> Made "Change Property" show conditionally.
It will no longer appear when a track's type does not have a property. (only property, blend_shape, and bezier have a property in the path)

If you call a subpath a property; If they are compatible, they should be changed path with keeping subpath, but if they are incompatible, just it should be aborted so it needs to validation process in somewhere, it is a not good implementation to remove them.

> No, normal PosRotScl3D track has ./Node3D as path, but PosRotScl3D with bone_pose uses subpaths separated by : like ./Skeleton3D:head.

Is there some demo project, documentation, or reproduction steps I can follow somewhere to set this up? I'm afraid i'm not familiar with the Skeleton3Ds and how they work with these tracks. I haven't been able to figure out how to reproduce this locally so far.

The extent of my testing have been using the "Add Track" button on various nodes, changing the node path / subpath of the track, and verifying the resulting path looks correct. Comparing it to the current workflow of typing in a path. This is where I got the idea PosRotScl3D tracks had no subpaths, but now I'm understanding there's a workflow with special behavior.

I've also never used BlendShape tracks before. In the context of the node paths, I've found they behave similarly to property and Bezier tracks, except they require 3D nodes to be selected. 

> Also, since subpaths are used not only on the Pos/Rot/Scl/Blendshape but also on the Bezier track, like ./Node2D/position:x, it would be necessary to test on the bezier track as well.

I've tested Bezier tracks in a sense I added a bezier track, changed the node/subpath, similar to the property track. It's currently treated similarly to the property/value track, in a sense it tends to have a subpath and either the node path or subpath can be changed.

In short, a track may have three attributes, not two as you seem to think like path and property.

- ObjectPath
- Property
- SubPath
  - A. property of the reference `./MeshInstance3D:surface_material_override/0:albedo_color`
  - B. element of the property `./Node2D/position:x`
  - C. bone `./Skeleton3D:head`
  - D. blendshape `./MeshInstance3D:smile`

So at first, we should implement a common method somewhere to parse the structure of the subpaths. Then you should provide different behavior for different cases by determining what the subpaths indicate:

In case A, you should provide the Variant type of the property that is the target of the subpath. This should be no so different than the normal behavior of selecting a ValueTrack property.

In case B, you should provide a filtered list of compatible properties by reference to the Variant type of the parent property.

In case C/D, you should provide a selector for bones and blendshapes.

This has been stuck for almost 2 years. What's the problem with allowing this option only for some track types? It's not like support for other types can't be added later. The initial PR could handle the most common types.

Even in the most commonly used value track, there are cases where the subpaths A and B mentioned above are utilized.

> SubPath
A. property of the reference ./MeshInstance3D:surface_material_override/0:albedo_color
B. element of the property ./Node2D/position:x

If there are no issues with the behavior in those two cases, it might be acceptable to allow this only in the value track. In particular, I remember the case of B, which accessed Variant's element via subpaths, was just a hack then, but since a feature was added to display them as a general option in the ValueTrack pop-up dialog (I remember it hes been added by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97563, and I fixed in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107241), safety standards may have become stricter since then.

> B. element of the property ./Node2D/position:x This is supported. The property dialog allows picking sub-properties, so you can change sub-property to another The only unsupported case are sub-properties that include other objects, like in your A example. The only problem is that the dialog does not include validation right now, but that's also something that can be improved later.

I like the idea of omitting some track types, I think the Transform tracks (Position3D/Rotation3D/Scale3D) add most of the edge cases. 
- Path to only nodes change node like normal
- Path to bones Change Node to only Skeleton3D
- Path to bones Change Target Bone with a BonePicker dialog.

I'll take a look this weekend with omitting some track types in mind.

I suppose omitting these tracks would involve just not showing the dialog box on that track type? Or perhaps graying it out or showing a warning when it is clicked?

I did notice an edge case while testing, where using the dialog to modify tracks using Unique Paths swapped out the `%` syntax with local node syntax like regular paths. I replicated it with AnimationPlayer/Add Track in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/120921. Not sure if it blocks this PR, but in hindsight maybe not.

The main thing I have left to implement is what to do when we change node and the property is then invalid.
my main idea was just prompting the user if they want to select a different property then opening PropertySelector like change target property. 

Now I'm wondering if there's a simpler approach to reduce the scope. Perhaps just let the user "Change Target Node", and if it doesn't land on a valid property they can follow up with "Change Target Property" manually. Would that be acceptable?

I worked on the Variant filters for the property selector recently, I think it's working but I'll have to retest everything and push changes. 

I'll take a look this weekend, I should have some extra time to dig into it.

While working on the filtering for "Change Target Property..." I found that the filter for the PropertyDialog doesn't currently support nested properties. For example, if I change target property on `position.x` it will set the filter to the Variant "float" and we get a window that looks like this: So only floats, no Vector2's, which contain float subproperties. Fixing this would require refactoring the PropertySelector and how it displays/filters the property list. I played around with this and it seems to be doable, but it's a wider change that I would be more comfortable leaving for a separate PR. I'd also like to avoid holding this PR up longer than it has to. I could write up a separate issue for it. Leaving the filters turned on prevents switching between sub-properties, but leaving them turned on makes it work fine. Still trying to get the changes pushed but I'll need to give it another sanity test first, when I get a chance.

OK, I've pushed what I have so far. 

Recent version has:
- Change Target Node now works for nested / referenced properties
- Change Target Node filters on Node type for required tracks, similarly to Add Track
	- Includes Skeleton3D filter for bone paths.
- "Change Target BlendShape" now appears in place of "Change Target Property" for BlendShape tracks, displays a PropertySelector filtered on floats similar to adding a new BlendShape track. I think I'm going to write up a quick issue for the current setup.
	- This now correctly changes the BlendShape path. 
- "Change Target Bone" appears, but throws a warning dialog indicating it's unimplemented.
- I've reordered the functions to match the header file.


A few outstanding issues that potentially gate the PR:
- Change Target Node, into a node that doesn't have the property doesn't do any validation. Didn't get around to the reprompt setup I was imagining. The user _could_ just manually "Change Target Property" in this scenario.
- I tried filtering the PropertySelector for "Change Target Property" but it prevented switching between sub-properties like position.x -> position.y. Filtering on floats hide Vector2's that contain floats. I plan to write up a separate issue for it, and left it out of the current version.
- Logic for "Change Target Bone" was put in, but I didn't get around to implementing the BonePicker. So it just throws a warning dialog when you click it. This is more to demonstrate current behavior, we'll probably want to hide the button altogether though.
- Change Target Node on a Unique node path `%MyNode:property` will not use the `%` in the new target node if it's unique.

I just updated the PR with some of the review comments, need some clarification on the bezier comment though. - Now prevents retargeting to the current animation in three cases: - AnimationPlayback Track, change node to self - Property track of current_animation, change node to self - Property track of arbitrary property on self, change target property to current_animation - new ints default to -1 - Cleaned up switch case to an if statement - Split up DIALOG_ enums into a seperate enum "DialogAction" - I'm not familiar with when to use anonymous enums so I gave it a name. - Removed unused menu enums "MENU_CHANGE_TARGET_BLENDSHAPE" and "MENU_CHANGE_TARGET_BONE" - Updated the BezierTrack property filtering, didn't realize earlier they only take numeric types. One thing I still need clarification is the bezier comment from @KoBeWi > Also you can change one component of a Bezier track. The editor still works, but it tries to force a numeric value in whatever property you selected. Ideally all related Bezier properties should get changed at once. I'm not overly familiar with the usage of the Bezier tracks, but from what I can tell: - Adding a new track filters for numeric types and vectors that contain them. - Adding a vector such as Vector2 splits it up into its components, and creates separate tracks with each. - These are mixed with other tracks and the tracks for a vector are not uniquely combined in any way I can tell, outside of just comparing the paths. In this case, change target property moving just the one track is consistent with the rest of the behavior, but I do see how we'd want the option to move other components of the vector along with it. Perhaps when we attempt to "Change Target Property" on a component of a vector, we should check if there are other tracks of the same vector, and prompt the user to see if they want to move the rest? "Would you like to move the entire Vector2 or just the x component?" And what if there's multiple components but not all? like rgb and not a? Or perhaps more similar to your suggestion, just automatically open a PropertySelector filtered for the correct vector type if there are ALL other components for the vector present as tracks. I'd be a bit concerned it's not obvious what the user is selecting, as the Change Target Property dialog doesn't show a description like what is the old target track we're changing.

> Perhaps when we attempt to "Change Target Property" on a component of a vector, we should check if there are other tracks of the same vector, and prompt the user to see if they want to move the rest?
> Or perhaps more similar to your suggestion, just automatically open a PropertySelector filtered for the correct vector type if there are ALL other components for the vector present as tracks.

I think the second option would be better. For more clarity, you could try experimenting with changing the title of property selector dialog.
And this should work for any bezier track. Basically, the track type is bezier, show property dialog for the base property, regardless if all components are present, then after picking, replace base path for all components.
I mean, when you create a bezier track, by default it adds all components, so changing the property should also be expected to change all components. To have incomplete bezier track you need to manually remove some components. (and removed components should not be restored when changing base path)

I've pushed two changes to my branch. 1. The title of both dialogs now includes the affected track path It's a bit odd to say "Select X to replace {path}" with the full path, if we're swapping just the node or property. But it seems ideal to have the context of the entire nodepath to indicate the specific track getting moved. I also dropped trailing colons as they're confusing with a nodepath in the title. I've also adjusted the Add Track's dialog to use title casing "Pick a node to animate:" -> "Pick a Node to Animate:" to align it with the other titles, but i'm open to switching it back for whatever reason. I did notice one uses "Pick a Node" and "Select Property" so I maintained "Pick" for the SceneTreeDialog and "Select" for the PropertyDialog. 2. Change Target Node for Bezier tracks will move the entire vector if all components are present and there are no duplicates. Implementing this for Change Target Property will take a bit more time, but the main logic is testable here. My current plan for Change Target Property will be to filter for the specific vector if moving the entire vector, and filtering for numeric types when moving the scalar, and raising a warning/error dialog if the user tries to move scalar into a vector. I also plan to write up a proposal for improving the filtering of the PropertySelector. Perhaps a separate proposal to support picking properties of references might make sense as well?
